suggestions.description: Page-jump surfaces draw their top separator inside the page grid.

evidence.summary: Paperwhite and Scribe library reports place a separator inside page-button rows instead of at the surface top. Paperwhite ToC and Scribe portrait/landscape ToC pickers reproduce it with expanded grids. In Scribe portrait the rule crosses the first row near y854; in landscape it crosses near y545 while the heading is near y468. The reports consistently distinguish this rule from the required top boundary.

suggestions.recommendation: Measure the complete jump surface from its title, padding, and every grid row, keep its white interior opaque, and anchor the 2 px rule above the title at the actual top edge. Cover any stale underlying separator while preserving the balanced grid, folio, and navigation allocations.

suggestions.description: Library More menus use incomplete or incorrect action icons.

evidence.summary: Both reports describe a standalone multiselect check in place of the reference checked square. The Scribe report additionally describes a bulleted-list glyph where the category-management row should have a folder outline; popup geometry and labels remain aligned.

suggestions.recommendation: Use the checked-square multiselect icon and the folder-outline category icon in their existing monochrome slots without changing row alignment.

suggestions.description: Paperwhite library filter-chip labels and widths are smaller than the reference.

evidence.summary: The source report estimates 14 px labels and 81 px chip widths versus approximately 16 px and 86 px in the normalized reference. The four-chip row ends about 20 px early while its height and surrounding sort geometry remain intact.

suggestions.recommendation: Match the reference label size and chip widths while retaining the approximately 44 px height and clear spacing.

suggestions.description: Source update rows omit the installed-to-available version transition.

evidence.summary: The Paperwhite report shows installed versions only; the Scribe report shows target versions only. Both report that the same captured state contains installed v12/v8 and available v13/v9, so the complete transition can be displayed from real records.

suggestions.recommendation: Build each update subtitle from matching installed and available source records and display both versions with an arrow while preserving existing update controls and profile geometry.

suggestions.description: Active incognito status strips omit the centered no-history policy notice.

evidence.summary: Paperwhite and Scribe reference reviews describe an inverted strip whose center is empty despite an active incognito preference. Supplemental reports reproduce the omission on both profiles after navigation and persistence, including detail routes without a history-page toggle. The issue concerns normal application pages; the closed-reader artwork-only exception remains explicit.

suggestions.recommendation: Render a concise centered incognito/no-history notice whenever incognito mode is active on normal application pages, including restored sessions. Preserve clock/device indicators and the artwork-only closed-reader exception.

suggestions.description: The Paperwhite description body lacks the specified first-line indent and line spacing.

evidence.summary: The revised report retains only this independently specified typography discrepancy: candidate lines are reported about 26 px apart with an unindented first line, versus the prototype's 18/32 body and two-em indent. No clipping or functional loss is reported.

suggestions.recommendation: Apply the two-em first-line indent and approximately 32 px line height while preserving content margins and content-driven sheet height.

suggestions.description: Enabled Paperwhite contrast controls lose their reference emphasis.

evidence.summary: The report describes pale minus/plus outlines and a regular-weight Standard label instead of black outlines and a bold value. The recorded contrast value is not at an endpoint.

suggestions.recommendation: Use black outlines for enabled contrast step buttons and the reference bold value treatment.

suggestions.description: All three reading-mode panels omit the reference slot for the independent wide-page splitting control.

evidence.summary: The original reports describe a missing row beneath crop borders on Paperwhite and an empty corresponding area beside crop borders in Scribe portrait and landscape. These observations establish missing structure; the latest scope accepts unintegrated splitting behavior when it is honestly unavailable.

suggestions.recommendation: Restore the independently labeled splitting-control slot and reference spacing in each reading-mode panel. While splitting is not integrated, show the control disabled with a concise accurate unavailable explanation. Do not present an enabled or successful state without real behavior.

suggestions.description: Paperwhite manual orientation omits reverse landscape.

evidence.summary: The report describes only Portrait and Landscape cards, corroborated by the recorded modal item IDs. The reference and expected state require a third manual reverse-landscape choice; sensor absence does not exclude it.

suggestions.recommendation: Implement and expose a real reverse-landscape state with the third enabled card and reference three-column geometry.

suggestions.description: Reading-mode title rows omit the current book's stored default-direction hint.

evidence.summary: Both reports describe an empty supporting-text area where the reference displays the book default, despite recorded right-to-left state and an enabled remember-book-direction preference.

suggestions.recommendation: Show the actual stored book-default direction with the reference subdued, right-aligned supporting-text treatment.

suggestions.description: The Paperwhite power page adds excess vertical space before the screensaver preview grid.

evidence.summary: The report identifies an approximately 8.5 px localized excess gap after an otherwise matching policy-row divider. Preview heights and horizontal dimensions match, and the explicit prototype gap and label tokens support the retained observation.

suggestions.recommendation: Match the 10 px main gap and 8 px label top margin with the appropriate 12 px line box while retaining the existing 150 px preview heights.

suggestions.description: Empty source preferences fail to produce a contained, recognizable source-settings state.

evidence.summary: For an empty source_preference_groups array, the Paperwhite report describes no visible settings change or dismissal action. The Scribe report describes a title, Done action, and empty message without the white outlined popover, exposing them against catalog controls.

suggestions.recommendation: Always render a white outlined source-settings container with source identity, a truthful empty-state message, appropriate internal padding, and a reachable Done/Close action. Size it to actual content and never fabricate preferences.

suggestions.description: The blocked-source recovery state omits its direct migration action.

evidence.summary: The report describes Source management and Uninstall without the reference migration action, while the captured state records migration_available=true.

suggestions.recommendation: Expose a direct action into the real migration flow. Where no migratable entries exist, show an accurate disabled state or explanation while retaining source switching and uninstall.

suggestions.description: Scribe server-setup actions have unequal widths.

evidence.summary: The report estimates a 359/269 px split where the reference uses two approximately 314 px actions, with no clipping pressure or meaningful label-length difference.

suggestions.recommendation: Give phone entry and test/connect equal flexible widths within the current form, retaining the existing gap, height, and truthful enabled or disabled state.

suggestions.description: The source picker truncates the distinguishing server connection state.

evidence.summary: The report describes Komga, Kavita, and Suwayomi showing the same generic category prefix and ellipsis, although the captured state distinguishes connected from unconfigured servers. The paired reference keeps those states readable.

suggestions.recommendation: Reserve a compact area for the complete actual connection/configuration state, truncating a generic category prefix first if needed.

suggestions.description: The Scribe queue panel border does not enclose its pagination.

evidence.summary: The reference review describes side borders stopping near y729 while the folio is below them near y765. Supplemental cancel and three-row operational frames reproduce this. A two-row final page also stops the outline near y622 with the folio near y656, so varying job counts do not remove the containment defect.

suggestions.recommendation: Include header, actual rows, pagination, and bottom padding in one content-sized white queue panel with a continuous four-sided outline on first and last pages and operation variants.

suggestions.description: The Scribe category-strip baseline has gaps beneath inactive tabs.

evidence.summary: The report describes white breaks in the thin gray divider beneath inactive tab cells, while the reference keeps a continuous baseline under the active underline.

suggestions.recommendation: Draw the shared divider after inactive tab backgrounds or confine those backgrounds above it, preserving tab geometry and the active underline.

suggestions.description: The manga More menu omits Delete all downloads when downloads exist.

evidence.summary: The report describes four menu rows where the reference has a fifth deletion row. Recorded modal items omit deletion even though downloaded_count=9.

suggestions.recommendation: Expose the contextual deletion action for the current book and connect it to the actual operation and required confirmation. If unavailable, retain a clearly disabled action with an accurate reason.

suggestions.description: The manga More menu omits leading action icons and shifts its text gutter left.

evidence.summary: The report describes text-only rows starting around logical x588 where the reference has icon slots and labels around x626. It records an approximately 38 px gutter shift, separately from the missing deletion row.

suggestions.recommendation: Restore consistent monochrome leading icons and the reference label gutter while retaining truthful gray unavailable states.

suggestions.description: The landscape Layout sheet omits separate-cover and whole/split-spread control structure.

evidence.summary: The original Layout report describes both control groups absent from the right column, with only the Single, Double, and Automatic page-layout items recorded. The Settings reports formerly grouped here instead show gray controls plus a visible unavailable label; those observations are preserved and accepted separately as P3R1-A01.

suggestions.recommendation: Restore labeled separate-cover and whole/split-spread control slots in the landscape Layout sheet. Show them disabled with a concise accurate unavailable explanation while the behaviors are not integrated, or reflect real state if a behavior exists. Preserve access alongside the three page-layout cards without implying successful unsupported behavior.

suggestions.description: The Scribe landscape orientation card does not communicate landscape spread.

evidence.summary: The report describes a generic Landscape label and single-page rectangle where the reference uses Landscape spread with a two-page icon. Captured state already records spread=true, so the observation concerns the affordance rather than demonstrated runtime behavior.

suggestions.recommendation: Use the landscape-spread label and divided two-page icon for the Scribe landscape action.

suggestions.description: Search result-card captions use serif rather than interface sans-serif typography.

evidence.summary: The report describes serif stroke contrast and terminals in all visible result captions beneath MangaDex and Komga covers, unlike the reference UI glyphs. It distinguishes this from the intentionally serif editing-state local-match heading.

suggestions.recommendation: Apply the reference sans-serif family and approximately 16 px caption weight to result cards while retaining the existing caption geometry and editing-state heading style.

suggestions.description: The failed-source Retry control is wider than the reference.

evidence.summary: The report estimates an 88 px candidate width versus approximately 74 px in the normalized reference, with matching short labels, 44 px height, and aligned right edge.

suggestions.recommendation: Use the reference width or equivalent horizontal padding while retaining height and right alignment.

suggestions.description: Unavailable category creation and renaming lack explicit action and capability presentation.

evidence.summary: The Scribe report describes missing disabled Rename affordances and counts occupying their trailing space. Paperwhite reports describe disabled New category and static category rows without visible unavailable status. The captured rows are disabled; the observations do not require simulated success.

suggestions.recommendation: Show a concise unavailable status for creation and renaming and retain appropriate disabled Rename and New category affordances. Keep actual counts, place counts before trailing actions, and preserve immutable Uncategorized. Implement real operations only if included in the product scope.

suggestions.description: Disabled logging settings omit the recorded visible unavailable feedback.

evidence.summary: Both profile reports describe disabled log controls and no visible explanation, although settings_status contains an unavailable message. The absence of that user-visible status remains actionable; the original request to implement logging operations is superseded by the latest scope.

suggestions.recommendation: Display the actual unavailable status and a concise reason where known beside the logging controls. Keep unsupported controls honestly disabled. Real logging integration may enable them later, but it is not required to resolve this feedback issue.

suggestions.description: Disabled charging-update and reading-time Wi-Fi rows lack a visible unavailable explanation.

evidence.summary: The targeted coordinator report confirms that the visible Unavailable label is beside the screensaver heading and applies only to its three disabled cards. The separate charging-update and reading-time Wi-Fi rows above it are disabled without visible explanation. This resolves the prior explanation-scope uncertainty while preserving the accepted screensaver limitation in A02.

suggestions.recommendation: Add a concise accurate unavailable explanation that clearly applies to each unsupported upper policy or to their shared group. Preserve honest disabled controls and the existing screensaver limitation. No unintegrated firmware or background policy implementation is required.

suggestions.description: Scribe logging action buttons are narrower than the reference.

evidence.summary: The report estimates approximately 100 px per button versus 118 px in the normalized reference and explicitly distinguishes the geometry difference from disabled operation state.

suggestions.recommendation: Restore the reference horizontal padding or minimum width while retaining left alignment and inter-button spacing.

suggestions.description: Storage settings omit the four-part usage presentation and largest-storage management section.

evidence.summary: Both profile reports describe only download/cache/free text and cleanup buttons, with no separate cover usage, stacked usage bar and legend, or largest-book rows/explicit empty state. Actual zero or unknown totals do not account for the missing structure.

suggestions.recommendation: Render download, cache, cover, and free totals from maintained real data with the usage visualization. Add real largest-storage records and targeted actions or a concise empty state, preserving cleanup and avoiding normal-projection filesystem scans.

suggestions.description: The shared Scribe device header truncates its capability summary before orientation is readable.

evidence.summary: The report describes the same ellipsized capability line across all four assigned settings cases. The reference fits its full summary before the status divider; actual wording may differ but essential capability information is incomplete.

suggestions.recommendation: Use concise truthful capability labels or rebalance header text width so the complete summary fits alongside the existing status column.

suggestions.description: Muted L-shaped and swipe-only layout cards lack an explicit truthful availability explanation.

evidence.summary: The original reports describe gray labels, indicators, and diagrams for the two alternatives and contrast that with the enabled reference examples. That visual observation is retained, but gray appearance alone is not a requirement to enable unintegrated mappings.

suggestions.recommendation: Keep the reference card structure and make the alternatives' actual availability clear. If unsupported, retain disabled styling with a concise accurate reason; if a real mapping is implemented, show its actual selectable and persistent state. Do not use normal enabled black styling merely to imply a working layout.

suggestions.description: The narrow installed-source row truncates its explicit unavailable status.

evidence.summary: The reference source-manager report and supplemental language/boundary frames describe the blocked subtitle ellipsizing after browser-verification wording before its explicit unavailable clause. Scribe 3 reproduces the same projection in its native stretched viewport. available=false and the full reason are recorded; warning styling and Uninstall remain visible. This remains a status-readability issue and does not require enabling the source.

suggestions.recommendation: Shorten the reason or reserve a concise visible unavailable segment before optional detail inside the 400 px installed column. Preserve the truthful browser-verification limitation, warning tile, and Uninstall action.

suggestions.description: Catalog include/exclude tags use plus/minus instead of the specified check/cross marks across profiles.

evidence.summary: The Paperwhite report records plus/minus prefixes for included and excluded Adventure. Scribe supplemental reports independently record the same glyph mismatch. Selected black surfaces and dashed/struck exclusion remain distinguishable, so these are marker-fidelity observations.

suggestions.recommendation: Use check and cross prefixes across profiles while retaining tri-state behavior, real counts, inverse inclusion, and dashed/struck-through exclusion.

suggestions.description: Dense tag collections truncate the text needed to distinguish actual filter and summary tags.

evidence.summary: Paperwhite first, second, and final filter pages collapse distinct numbered tags or included labels to common prefixes. Scribe reports the same loss across all three filter pages and the summary's visible tag collection, with 34 distinct tag identities retained in case data.

suggestions.recommendation: Reflow or resize tag controls, use fewer columns or additional pages, and preserve each short distinguishing suffix plus its include/exclude marker. Let short final pages use available width. Keep this identity issue distinct from labels painting outside detail chip outlines in G40.

suggestions.description: Description pagination splits English words at page boundaries.

evidence.summary: The report records one page ending with the first letter of provider and the following page starting with its remaining letters. It explicitly does not assert lost text.

suggestions.recommendation: Prefer word or paragraph boundaries while preserving every character and content-driven final-sheet height.

suggestions.description: View all hides settled source results behind an inconsistent setup gate.

evidence.summary: The Paperwhite report describes a blank catalog despite 40 recorded results and pagination. The Scribe report describes a setup form with no cards or folio despite 40 results and ten visible_catalog records in state. Both record source_needs_setup=true. A separate Scribe server-connect frame does display a populated catalog, so the observation is specific to the View-all flow rather than a global rendering failure.

suggestions.recommendation: Reconcile setup state with the actual fetched catalog when entering from View all and present returned records with pagination. If setup genuinely prevents their use, show a specific truthful reason and usable recovery action without fabricating a verified connection or needlessly requiring repeated setup.

suggestions.description: Offline/demo library refresh reports Saved instead of the actual update-check outcome.

evidence.summary: The Paperwhite report describes a Saved toast in the demo/offline branch that returns before an update check or save. The Scribe report reproduces the unrelated Saved acknowledgement with offline=true and busy=false, noting that its mechanical check accepts any nonempty message rather than validating refresh semantics.

suggestions.recommendation: Show explicit offline/demo feedback when updates were not checked. For real requests, show checking only while actual work runs and then the actual completion/error result. Preserve the compact outlined toast without fabricated success.

suggestions.description: The download destination is truncated before its identifying directory components.

evidence.summary: The report describes a single ellipsized Save location value ending after the shared run-directory prefix. The complete actual path exists in recorded settings data, but its row is disabled and has no full-path action.

suggestions.recommendation: Wrap the destination in a dedicated multiline value area or provide a visible full-path detail action on Paperwhite.

suggestions.description: Add source list uses a solid border instead of the creation-action dashed outline.

evidence.summary: The report describes Add source list and Open source management with matching solid outlines, while HANDOFF and static prototype text distinguish dashed creation actions from solid management actions.

suggestions.recommendation: Apply the declared white dashed-outline treatment to Add source list and retain the solid management action.

suggestions.description: Empty Bookmarks tabs provide a blank list without status or a clear next step.

evidence.summary: Paperwhite, Scribe portrait, and Scribe landscape reports describe a selected Bookmarks tab followed by blank white list space, zero bookmark records, and no explanatory status or understandable next step. The header bookmark control exists, but the empty list does not identify it.

suggestions.recommendation: Show a concise no-bookmarks status and an understandable next step based on actual state, such as a labeled current-page bookmark action or guidance identifying the existing header control. Retain the content-sized white sheet and undimmed artwork.

suggestions.description: Scribe detail metadata tags overflow their chip outlines and omit undisclosed values.

evidence.summary: Queue-exposed and content-stress detail reports describe Adventure, Long metadata, and numbered tag labels painting outside narrow boxes and colliding. Real-migration candidate, selected, and committed reports reproduce that containment issue and record five actual tags while only four compressed chips are visible, with no second row or overflow disclosure.

suggestions.recommendation: Measure every label plus horizontal padding, wrap the complete chip collection inside the information column with distinct gaps, and let its height follow the rows. Preserve every actual tag or expose an operable overflow disclosure if a limit is intentional; keep oversized text within its own bounds.

suggestions.description: Installed-source truncation removes the distinguishing suffix from adjacent real configurations.

evidence.summary: The report describes the first ten saved sources as the same Configured local fixture 0... prefix with identical tiles/status, although actual names contain distinct 00 and 01 suffixes within 25 configurations.

suggestions.recommendation: Preserve the unique part of long source names through wrapping, additional name allocation, or suffix-preserving truncation while retaining truthful connection status in the installed column.

suggestions.description: The Scribe description pager extends below the floating summary outline.

evidence.summary: The report describes final-page side rules ending near y739 while the 3/3 folio is near y774 on a white strip extending to roughly y807 with no closing bottom rule. The taller first page also leaves its description-pagination region unframed.

suggestions.recommendation: Include description pagination and its padding inside the panel's measured content height and draw continuous side and bottom rules around the complete white surface, allowing short final pages to shrink to content.

suggestions.description: The empty-history body provides a status without a direct next action.

evidence.summary: The empty-history and clear-apply reports both describe a clock icon and status heading with no nearby action. The clear endpoint records zero history, no modal, and a 1/1 folio. The global dock remains usable, but HANDOFF explicitly requires status plus an action in the empty component.

suggestions.recommendation: Add one concise real Library or Browse route action beneath the empty-history status, retaining centered monochrome presentation without explanatory body copy.

suggestions.description: The fourth searched source has no visible scope entry or overflow affordance.

evidence.summary: The report describes an All sources count of four but only three named controls for the empty, error, and fast fixtures. The slow group is visibly pending or populated in the two result frames and exists among four recorded search groups, yet there is no slow-source chip, More action, scope pager, or picker.

suggestions.recommendation: Provide a visible scope selector for every searchable source through readable named controls, a bounded picker, explicit overflow, or pagination. Make the slow source selectable in both pending and completed states.

suggestions.description: Migration candidates omit their match classification.

evidence.summary: The report describes three real candidate rows containing title and source/author text but no right-side exact or approximate match indicator. Current series-000 appears alongside candidates series-000, series-001, and series-002; HANDOFF and static prototype text specify a match indication.

suggestions.recommendation: Display a concise classification derived from reliable actual candidate metadata, such as exact normalized title or approximate title. If a trustworthy comparison is unavailable, state that explicitly instead of inventing a confidence score.

suggestions.description: PW6 catalog source metadata omits the known loaded or filtered-result count.

evidence.summary: The source report describes metadata containing language and version but no count. Its case data records catalog_count=128, five visible entries, and 26 pages. The coordinator accepts a P3 information-fidelity issue and explicitly distinguishes this known loaded/filtered set from any unverified provider-wide total.

suggestions.recommendation: Show the actual loaded count or known filtered-result count with a clear label such as Loaded or Known results. Use a remote total only when the provider explicitly supplies a reliable total. Never relabel catalog_count as the remote site's whole-catalog total.

suggestions.description: The dock has an extra thick dark segment spanning several inactive tabs.

evidence.summary: The targeted coordinator report records a candidate segment near logical x57-874 and y1162-1167. The normalized reference instead has a thin full-width top rule and a short selected Settings marker near x800-874. The responsible component is not established by the reported pixels.

suggestions.recommendation: Constrain the selected indicator to its intended tab and remove the extra long dark segment while retaining the required thin top rule. Inspect indicator geometry and any unintentionally exposed horizontal scrollbar without assuming the cause in advance.

summary: Every one of the 454 required current captures and all 110 original reference images was inspected. Forty-seven actionable UI groups remain. The original full round has one unsettled capture, unresolved captured-scope gaps, and pending Root-managed external evidence, so it is not a clean round.

review_method.context: Fresh child context per bounded image batch; no full-image-set context was inherited.
review_method.model_routing: Parent model intentionally inherited because advertised metadata did not distinguish model capabilities.
review_method.comparison: Native logical 1x captures and physical 2x references were compared at matching logical proportions; stretched profiles retain their own native viewports.
review_method.identity: Each conclusion is bound to the SHA256 of unmodified original PNG bytes. A changed PNG invalidates its prior review.
review_method.local_execution: Read and viewed existing evidence and authored review documents only. No local application, build, test, smoke test or runtime probe was executed.

observations: Viewed the original 990x1320 candidate. The sidecar identifies scribe3-nofrontlight, reader route, menu=true, no modal, and false frontlight/warmth declarations.

The open menu header separates the book/chapter title, bookmark, table of contents, and time/battery without a visible collision. The page indicator reads 12/40, consistent with the recorded reader position.

The bottom rail contains four evenly allocated tools for reading mode, image, direction, and More. The absent brightness tool leaves no disabled lighting entry or empty tool slot; no warmth control is exposed.

The progress track, square thumb, and RTL chapter actions remain legible above the tools. Artwork dots, crosshatching, and white panel gutters belong to the displayed illustration and are not an interface scrim or a claimed viewport inset.
intentional_differences: The absent light tool must be reviewed on the native menu; no imaginary hardware capability is enabled.
The 990x1320 Scribe 3 viewport is a native stretched profile, not an exact Scribe 1/2 reference canvas.
recorded_capture_intentional_differences: The absent light tool must be reviewed on the native menu; no imaginary hardware capability is enabled.

observations: Viewed the original 990x1320 settings capture. The actual profile is scribe3-nofrontlight with has_frontlight=false and has_warmth=false, matching the case identity.
The left navigation begins with screen/refresh, Wi-Fi/sleep/exit, and storage. There is no lighting navigation entry, dependent brightness/warmth row, or unsupported pen entry.

The fixed navigation pane and right detail pane remain separate. Refresh choices fit in one row with six pages selected; the three quality cards are visibly muted and explicitly labeled unavailable rather than showing fabricated active behavior.

The sixteen-step grayscale strip, rectangular switches, page title, and bottom settings navigation remain within their allocations. The UI uses white surfaces and rules without a shadow or dimmed mask.
intentional_differences: This real device profile declares no frontlight; dependent controls must be absent.
Unavailable software quality choices are shown with an unavailable label and disabled appearance. This is separate from hiding absent hardware capabilities.
The 990x1320 native viewport has no independent Scribe 3 reference PNG.
recorded_capture_intentional_differences: This real device profile declares no frontlight; dependent controls must be absent.

observations: At equal logical scale, the white continuation card is approximately x16..602 and y104..227, and the four-column, two-row cover grid starts around y291, matching the reference allocations.
Unread badges and downloaded icons remain next to book titles below the cover frames. All eight visible titles and their state markers fit without unintended clipping.

The heavy serif page and continuation titles, smaller body labels, black primary text, secondary gray text, and light gray progress track preserve the reference hierarchy. White interface surfaces show no offset shadow or stippled backdrop.
The centered folio remains around y727 above the 72 px dock, whose top is around y752. The next-page action and all five dock items remain visible.
intentional_differences: Cover artwork and raster detail differ from the reference artwork; cover-frame geometry and title-adjacent state placement were still reviewed.

observations: The full-width white queue sheet starts at approximately y423 in the candidate and y475 logical in the reference. Its header and three visible queue rows retain the reference-relative spacing, cover allocations, and progress-track geometry.

Three queue rows show complete cover frames, title/chapter text, progress tracks, and reserved right-side counter or waiting-state space. Long fixture titles ellipsize before the status allocation instead of colliding with it.
The pause-all and close controls remain fully visible in the header. The two-page folio and next-page control remain fully visible at the bottom, with no row or control clipping.
The heavy serif sheet title, body type, black progress fill, secondary gray status text, white surface, and plain top rule preserve the reference hierarchy without shadow or stippled overlay.
intentional_differences: Actual download workers produced a five-item queue and a two-page folio, while the reference contains three fixture queue entries. Titles, cover content, counters, progress, time, and library counts are data differences.

The candidate sheet is approximately 401 px high rather than the reference's 349 px because it adds the required 52 px folio. This is a supported content expansion: prototype/Main.dc.html:174 anchors the sheet at bottom:0 without a fixed height, and docs/DESIGN_HANDOFF.md:279-280 explicitly states that sheets follow content rather than fixed heights.
recorded_capture_intentional_differences: Queue records and progress are produced by actual download workers against delayed loopback image responses.

observations: The bottom-attached queue displays chapters 1, 2, and 3, each with a cover, an ellipsized title, a full progress rule, and a readable 6 / 6 page count. The title and right-side count do not overlap.
Pause all is visibly disabled, Close remains prominent, and the centered 1 / 2 folio preserves an empty previous-page allocation and a visible next-page control.
The sheet has a white background and black top rule without shadow, stippled backdrop, or dimming. The settings content behind it retains its normal contrast.

The case sidecar records four completed jobs and chapter 5 cancelled at 2 / 6. The supplied cancel-all check reports the real job update. The cancelled row is on the unshown second page, so this frame alone does not visually prove its status.
A content-height bottom sheet presents the Download management heading, a black Done action, and three separate rows for Continue reading, Remove offline chapter, and Cancel.
Each row label is fully readable with clear separators and no footer collision. The white sheet and black top rule preserve the undimmed settings page behind it.

The metadata identifies the menu as the completed chapter 1 job and enables only reading, removal, and close actions. The visible choices agree with that completed-job context; no active download progress is claimed.

The completed queue is open above the manga detail route rather than the settings route. The visible detail heading, artwork cover, continuation action, and directory heading remain undimmed above the sheet.
Chapters 1 through 3 each display a full progress rule and 6 / 6 pages. Long fixture chapter titles truncate before the separate count area and remain on one line.
The disabled Pause all action, enabled Close action, and 1 / 2 folio fit within the white sheet without clipping or shadow.

The supplied sidecar records the visible jobs as completed, with counts matching the rendered 6 / 6 labels. Actual completion is supported by that existing evidence, not by a newly executed operation in this review.
The reopened queue starts with chapters 2, 3, and 4; chapter 1 is absent from the visible membership. All three remaining visible rows show full progress and 6 / 6 pages.

The background storage summary displays 51 KB, while the before-removal and cancellation frames display 69 KB. This is consistent with the supplied removal evidence without asserting independent byte-level verification.
The 1 / 2 folio and next-page control remain aligned after the queue count changes from five to four. No blank duplicate row, title collision, or progress clipping is visible.
The sidecar records four remaining jobs, reports removal of the actual completed job, and records the chapter 1 downloaded flag as false. The screenshot provides the corresponding visible row update.
The confirmation has closed to the settings page, with no residual dialog outline, dimming, or stale overlay. The settings rows, 1 / 2 folio, and selected Settings dock item are readable.
The storage summary remains 69 KB, matching the retained-download state rather than the 51 KB removal-applied frame.
The supplied state has no active modal and still contains five jobs, including completed chapter 1 at 6 / 6. Its cancellation check reports preservation of the actual completed download.
The queue itself is not visible after cancellation, so file preservation and the retained row are metadata-supported observations rather than directly visible content in this frame.
A compact white outlined confirmation is fully contained within the viewport and leaves the settings background undimmed. Its border is clear without a shadow or stippled backdrop.
The prompt to remove this chapter download and retain shared or imported content fits on one line without cropping.
Cancel and Remove are equal-width adjacent actions with readable centered labels; the destructive action has the intended black fill and white text.
The supplied modal context identifies completed chapter 1, and its two action identifiers are job-remove-confirm and close. The visible confirmation agrees with that action state.

The second queue page contains two distinct rows for chapters 4 and 5, each with its own cover, truncated title, empty progress rule, and Waiting to download status. These labels agree with the zero-completed queued state in the sidecar.
The centered 2 / 2 folio exposes Previous page on the left and leaves the next-page edge allocation empty. No first-page row is repeated.
With two rows, the bottom sheet starts lower than the three-row queue frames. This follows the documented content-dependent sheet height and is not treated as a fixed-height mismatch.
Pause all and Close remain fully readable. The sheet, progress rules, separators, and undimmed settings backdrop show no overlap, clipping, shadow, or stipple.

applicable_constraints: Treat this as a behavioral and refresh specification board, not an application route or proof of working candidate behavior.

While a reader menu is open, page-turn zones are inactive. Tapping the center or the specified outside area closes the menu. At a chapter boundary, a next action enters the next chapter with the required full refresh.
Use fast A2/DU feedback only within the pressed control and restore it with a UI refresh on release.

Opening/closing reader chrome uses UI GL16 updates limited to the edge bars; the specified close-time flashui option is a real refresh setting, not an animation. Popups, dialogs, and toasts use UI GL16 for their own rectangle, keep the artwork/background undimmed, close on outside capture, and restore only the original rectangle.

List page/tab changes refresh the content and folio values while fixed headers and navigation remain stable. Page-grid expansion/collapse refreshes its panel above the folio; choosing a page coalesces the grid and list update.

Manga page turns use partial REAGL/GL16 updates, promoted to full after the selected interval. The shown default is every six turns, with 1, 3, 6, 10, or chapter-only choices. Entering the reader, changing chapters, and leaving a full-screen image use full GC16 to clear residuals.
Seeking updates page-number feedback while dragging; decode and display the destination only on release. The waveform progression is fast A2 to partial GL16.

Coalesce continued cover loading into 300 ms UI GL16 batches rather than repeatedly refreshing the entire page. Keyboard presses use fast DU feedback with the candidate strip refreshed as UI; inverse feedback should appear within 100 ms.

The declared refresh vocabulary is full/partial/ui/flashui/fast/a2. Unsupported waveform modes fall back to GL16. Report actual fallback behavior; a static PNG cannot establish waveform or timing compliance.
Night mode is declared as whole-screen display-driver inversion without redrawing the content. Expose that operation only where the actual driver supports it; do not infer support from the reference.

Tap activates on release. Long press is at least 500 ms. Double tap is under 300 ms, is unused in ordinary lists, and defaults off for reader zoom; enabling it entails the documented single-tap delay. Horizontal swipe is within 900 ms with at least 5.6 mm movement and follows reader direction. Reader pinch zoom refreshes fully on release; a downward gesture beginning in the top 8 mm opens the menu.

Use actual downloaded/offline state and actual integrations. An in-app Pinyin/English/numeric keyboard and supported phone/local input can replace absent system entry surfaces; source CAPTCHA, source setup, code/QR authentication, and connection success must never be simulated.

Keep image work bounded to the target display size, cache rendered 8-bit grayscale pixels, prefetch two pages, and decode long strips in chunks. Static component images provide no performance evidence.

Treat sleep as a Wi-Fi-disconnection boundary: downloads use actual keep-awake behavior, downloaded content remains readable offline, and automatic updates follow the stated charging-and-Wi-Fi condition.

Preserve the declared system coexistence and retained-artwork sleep behavior when actually supported. Emulator screenshots do not qualify physical sleep/wake, hardware inversion, e-ink waveforms, light, sensor, or pen behavior.
